title: Derived dual of a quotient by an invertible ideal
statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq S$ an ideal which, as an $S$-module, is finitely generated projective and locally free of rank one (after localization at every prime). Put $B=S/I$ with its quotient ring map, and put $N=\operatorname{Hom}_B(I\otimes_S B,B)$, the ordinary $B$-module dual of the scalar extension of $I$. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived coinduction $C_B^S$ with its specified $B$-action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. There is an isomorphism in $D(B)$
$$C_B^S(S[0])\ \cong\ N[0][-1].$$
No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed; $I=S$ and zero rings are allowed.

proof.text: Write $j:I\hookrightarrow S$, $q:S\twoheadrightarrow B$, and $I^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,S)$. Choose finite generators of $I$, giving a surjection $p:S^n\twoheadrightarrow I$. Projectivity, in the lifting formulation of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], gives $a:I\to S^n$ with $pa=1_I$. Thus $I$ is a direct summand of a finite free module, as required by [lem-trf-line-module-duality]. Its other hypothesis is exactly the assumed rank-one freeness at every prime. That node identifies the scalar map $c:S\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,I)$, $s\mapsto(x\mapsto sx)$, as an isomorphism. No trivialization of $I$ is chosen.

proof.text:
By the exact-Hom definition of projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applying $\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,-)$ to $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}S\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$ gives
$$0\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,I)\xrightarrow{j\circ-}I^\vee\xrightarrow{q\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,B)\to0.$$
Under $c$ of Step 1 its first map is $u:S\to I^\vee$, $u(s)(x)=sx$. In particular $u$ is injective. Identify the last term with $N$ by the explicit inverse maps
$$h\longmapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto b\,h(x)),\qquad \nu\longmapsto(x\mapsto\nu(x\otimes1)).$$
The first formula is balanced because $h(sx)=q(s)h(x)$; the second is $S$-linear for the same reason. Their composites are identities on $x$ and on the generating tensors $x\otimes b$. Hence $\operatorname{coker}(u)\cong N$ as $S$-modules. This step uses only exactness in the cited definition and the displayed tensor formulas.

proof.text: Take $E^{-1}=I$, $E^0=S$, $d_E^{-1}=-j$, and all other terms zero, augmented by $q$ to $B[0]$. Its negative cohomology is zero since $j$ is injective, and its degree-zero cohomology is $S/I=B$; thus the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Its terms are projective: $I$ by assumption, and $S$ because an $S$-linear map out of $S$ lifts along any surjection by lifting the image of $1$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Apply [lem-sc-derived-hom-projective-resolution] with $A=S,F=B,G=S$. It represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(B[0],S[0])$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E,S[0])$. The total-Hom differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] is $d(f)=d_{S[0]}f-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_E$. With our sign choice the resulting two-term complex is precisely $S\xrightarrow{u}I^\vee$ in degrees $0,1$. Step 2 therefore gives cohomology zero in every degree other than $1$, and degree-one cohomology $N$, as $S$-modules.

proof.text:
Put $K=C_B^S(S[0])\in D(B)$ and let $U$ be scalar restriction. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], $UK\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(B[0],S[0])$ in $D(S)$, with the action stipulated in [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Restriction of module scalars preserves kernels, images and quotients: each is the same subgroup with the restricted action. Consequently $U H^r(K)=H^r(UK)$, and a $B$-module is zero if its underlying $S$-module is zero. Step 3 implies $H^r(K)=0$ for $r\ne1$ and gives an $S$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:UH^1(K)\to UN$. This is automatically $B$-linear: for $b\in B$ choose $s\in S$ with $q(s)=b$; then for $z\in H^1(K)$,
$$\alpha(bz)=\alpha(sz)=s\alpha(z)=b\alpha(z).$$
The same applies to its inverse. Thus $H^1(K)\cong N$ as $B$-modules. This argument uses scalar restriction on cohomology only, and does not lift an arbitrary derived $S$-isomorphism to $D(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0A71, lemma-RHom-ext; Tag 0BZH, lemma-compute-for-effective-Cartier-algebraic, reduction of the single cohomology-module assertion by fully faithful ordinary module restriction.

proof.text: The shifted object $K[1]\in D(B)$ has $H^r(K[1])=H^{r+1}(K)$, so it is concentrated in degree zero and its degree-zero cohomology is $N$. Apply [lem-amb-derived-degree-zero-normalization] in the abelian category of $B$-modules to obtain $K[1]\cong H^0(K[1])[0]\cong N[0]$. Shifting back gives the required isomorphism $K\cong N[0][-1]$ in $D(B)$. The normalization also applies when $B$ is the zero ring. If $I=S$, the map $u$ is the identity after $\operatorname{Hom}_S(S,S)=S$, so both sides are zero; if $S=0$ this is the same zero-category case. If $I=0$, Step 1 forces $S\cong\operatorname{End}_S(0)=0$, so that case is already included.
